questions.q:
Consider the following statements about road development in India:
1. The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.
2. The North-South and East-West Corridors link Srinagar with Kanyakumari and Silchar with Porbandar.
3. The Golden Quadrilateral was built under the Bharatmala Pariyojana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both were part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), launched in 1998-99 by the NHAI. Bharatmala Pariyojana came in 2017 as a later umbrella programme, so the Golden Quadrilateral was not built under it.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Transport chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 8

questions.q:
Under the present National Highway numbering system, consider the following statements:
1. NH 44, connecting Srinagar and Kanyakumari, is the longest national highway.
2. North-South highways carry even numbers and East-West highways odd numbers.
3. NH 27 is part of the East-West Corridor between Porbandar and Silchar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: After the 2010 renumbering, even numbers run north-south (increasing from east to west) and odd numbers east-west (increasing from south to north). NH 44 (old NH 7) is the longest at about 3,700 km, and NH 27 is the East-West Corridor.
questions.s: MoRTH; Majid Husain, Transport chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian Railways:
1. The metre gauge has a width of 762 mm.
2. The first passenger train ran between Bombay (Bori Bunder) and Thane in 1853.
3. The broad gauge has a width of 1,676 mm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first line was opened on 16 April 1853 over about 34 km, and broad gauge measures 1,676 mm. Metre gauge is 1,000 mm; 762 mm (and 610 mm) is narrow gauge.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 8; Majid Husain

questions.q: The Konkan Railway, opened in 1998, passes through which one of the following sets of States?
questions.e: It runs from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur near Mangalore in Karnataka (about 740 km), cutting through the steep Western Ghats and numerous rivers via tunnels and bridges. It does not enter Kerala; beyond Mangalore, trains run on the Southern Railway network.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 8; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Match List-I (Railway Zone) with List-II (Headquarters) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. East Central Railway
B. South East Central Railway
C. West Central Railway
D. North Western Railway
List-II
1. Jaipur
2. Hajipur
3. Jabalpur
4. Bilaspur
questions.e: East Central Railway is at Hajipur (Bihar), South East Central at Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh), West Central at Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) and North Western at Jaipur (Rajasthan). Remember the compass prefix does not always reflect the headquarters' direction.
questions.s: Ministry of Railways; Majid Husain

questions.q:
How many of the following railways are inscribed together as 'Mountain Railways of India' on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
1. Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
2. Nilgiri Mountain Railway
3. Kalka-Shimla Railway
4. Matheran Hill Railway
questions.e: The Darjeeling line (1999), Nilgiri line (2005) and Kalka-Shimla line (2008) form the serial listing. Matheran Hill Railway is on India's tentative list but not inscribed.
questions.s: UNESCO World Heritage List; Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about National Waterways (NW):
1. NW-1 runs along the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly from Haldia to Prayagraj.
2. NW-3, the West Coast Canal from Kottapuram to Kollam, is in Tamil Nadu.
3. NW-2 lies on the Brahmaputra between Dhubri and Sadiya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NW-3 (West Coast Canal with the Udyogmandal and Champakara canals) is in Kerala, not Tamil Nadu. The Inland Waterways Authority of India develops these and has its headquarters at Noida.
questions.s: IWAI; Majid Husain, Transport chapter

questions.q: The Jal Marg Vikas Project, assisted by the World Bank, is intended for capacity augmentation of navigation on which one of the following waterways?
o: Haldia to Varanasi stretch of the Ganga (NW-1)
Dhubri to Sadiya stretch of the Brahmaputra (NW-2)
Kottapuram to Kollam West Coast Canal (NW-3)
questions.e: The project deepens and develops NW-1, India's longest national waterway, to allow vessels of 1,500-2,000 tonnes to carry cargo along the Ganga. NW-1 is also the first waterway declared a national waterway (1986).
questions.s: PIB; IWAI

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian ports:
1. Kandla was developed after Partition to replace the port of Karachi.
2. Paradip is a port on the east coast in Odisha.
3. Kolkata is a deep natural harbour on the open sea coast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kandla (Deendayal Port) in the Gulf of Kachchh was built to serve the Gujarat and northwest hinterland after Karachi went to Pakistan. Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hugli, 100+ km inland, and silting is a recurring problem that led to Haldia's development.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 8; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Statement-I: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) was developed to relieve congestion at Mumbai Port.
Statement-II: Mumbai Port is a natural harbour but has limited land for expansion because of the island city's geography.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Mumbai Port is hemmed in by the city and handles a large share of cargo, so a satellite port was built across the harbour at Nhava Sheva. JNPT is now India's largest container port.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 8; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ports in India:
1. All ports in India are administered by the Union Government.
2. Major ports are administered by the Central Government, while non-major ports are administered by the maritime boards or governments of the coastal States.
3. Mundra is a non-major port.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Entry 27 of the Union List covers ports declared major, while non-major ports are handled by the State Maritime Boards under the Concurrent List. The Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 replaced the Major Port Trusts Act of 1963 for the major ports; Mundra in Gujarat is a non-major private port.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Seventh Schedule; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about civil aviation in India are correct?
1. The UDAN scheme was launched in 2012.
2. The first UDAN flight operated between Shimla and Delhi in 2017.
3. The Airports Authority of India was formed in 1995 by merging the National Airports Authority and the International Airports Authority of India.
4. Air India was nationalised in 1947.
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik, the Regional Connectivity Scheme) was launched in October 2016, and Air India was nationalised in 1953 under the Air Corporations Act.
questions.s: Ministry of Civil Aviation; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about pipelines in India:
1. The Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur pipeline carries natural gas.
2. The Salaya-Mathura pipeline carries natural gas.
3. The Naharkatiya-Barauni pipeline was the first cross-country crude oil pipeline in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: HBJ is a gas trunk line linking western gas fields to fertilizer plants in the north. Salaya-Mathura is a crude oil line feeding the Mathura refinery from Gujarat; Naharkatiya (Assam) to Barauni was the first crude pipeline, laid in the early 1960s.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Transport chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 8

questions.q: Which one of the following was the first city in India to start a metro rail service?
questions.e: Kolkata's metro opened in 1984 (Dum Dum-Tollygunge stretch). Delhi's followed in 2002 and became far larger in network.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Transport chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about trade passes along the northern borders:
1. Nathu La in Sikkim connects India with Tibet and trade through it was reopened in 2006.
2. Lipulekh is a pass in Uttarakhand used in trade with Tibet.
3. Shipki La, through which the Sutlej enters India, is in Uttarakhand.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Shipki La is in Himachal Pradesh (Kinnaur), where the Sutlej enters India from Tibet. Nathu La (Sikkim) and Lipulekh (Uttarakhand) are both used for border trade with Tibet.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Transport chapter; MEA

questions.q:
How many of the following land customs stations are correctly paired with the neighbouring country and Indian State?
1. Attari-Wagah : Pakistan, Punjab
2. Moreh-Tamu : Myanmar, Mizoram
3. Raxaul-Birgunj : Nepal, Bihar
4. Petrapole-Benapole : Bangladesh, Assam
questions.e: Attari-Wagah (Punjab) and Raxaul-Birgunj (Bihar) are correct. Moreh is in Manipur, and Petrapole is in West Bengal, which handles the bulk of the land trade with Bangladesh.
questions.s: Ministry of Home Affairs (LPAI); Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following has been the largest single item of India's merchandise imports by value in most years of the last two decades?
questions.e: India imports most of its crude oil because domestic production meets only a small share of demand, so crude oil and petroleum products dominate the import bill. Gold and electronics rank lower in most years.
questions.s: Economic Survey; Ministry of Commerce (Export-Import data)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP):
1. The United States is a member of RCEP.
2. India decided not to join the RCEP agreement in November 2019.
3. Japan and China are both members of RCEP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India withdrew from the negotiations over concerns about a widening trade deficit with China and insufficient market access. RCEP includes the ten ASEAN countries plus China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand, and the United States is not a member.
questions.s: MEA / PIB statements, Nov 2019; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about cropping seasons in India:
1. Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested in September-October.
2. Rabi crops depend mainly on the south-west monsoon rainfall.
3. Zaid crops are grown in the short season between rabi and kharif, for example watermelon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rabi crops are sown in winter (October-December) and harvested in April-June; they rely on irrigation and winter rain from western disturbances rather than the monsoon. Rice, cotton and jute are kharif crops; wheat, gram and mustard are rabi.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Match List-I (Shifting cultivation name) with List-II (Region) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Jhum
B. Podu
C. Bewar
D. Kumari
List-II
1. Madhya Pradesh
2. Western Ghats
3. North-eastern India
4. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
questions.e: Jhum is the North-east's slash-and-burn cultivation, Podu is used in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, Bewar in Madhya Pradesh and Kumari in the Western Ghats. In all of them the forest is burnt, cultivated for a few years and then left fallow to recover.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Agriculture chapter; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the climatic requirements of crops:
1. Wheat is grown in regions receiving about 50 to 75 cm of annual rainfall.
2. Cotton grows well in a warm climate with a long frost-free period, on black soil.
3. Jute needs a cool and dry climate with low rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Jute, a golden-fibre crop of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, needs hot, humid conditions and high rainfall (over 120 cm), not a cool dry climate. Wheat suits cool winters with moderate rain, and cotton thrives on moisture-retentive black soil.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Majid Husain

questions.q: Dry farming in India is mainly practised in regions that receive annual rainfall of less than about 75 cm. Which of the following sets of crops is best suited to such regions?
questions.e: Dry farming depends on moisture conservation and drought-resistant crops, mostly millets, pulses and oilseeds. Rice, jute, sugarcane and the plantation crops need high rainfall or assured irrigation.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Statement-I: Tank irrigation is more common in peninsular India than in the northern plains.
Statement-II: The peninsular terrain has hard, impervious rock, undulating land and non-perennial rivers, which favour storing water in tanks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Hard rock prevents seepage, so wells are less effective, and the uneven land lets small bunds hold runoff for the dry months. The northern plains have soft alluvium and plentiful groundwater, so tubewells and canals dominate there.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Majid Husain
questions.h: Hard rock = tanks, soft alluvium = tubewells

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cropping intensity is the ratio of net sown area to gross cropped area, multiplied by 100.
2. Net sown area is the area on which crops are sown, counting land cropped more than once as a single area.
3. Gross cropped area is the net sown area plus the area sown more than once.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cropping intensity = gross cropped area / net sown area x 100, so a value above 100 shows multiple cropping. Statement 1 has the ratio the wrong way round.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Match List-I (Revolution) with List-II (Sector) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Operation Flood
B. Blue Revolution
C. Yellow Revolution
D. Golden Revolution
List-II
1. Fisheries
2. Horticulture
3. Oilseeds
4. Milk
questions.e: Operation Flood (1970, NDDB, V. Kurien) is the White Revolution in milk; Blue is fish, Yellow is oilseeds and Golden is horticulture. These Revolutions followed the Green Revolution in food grains.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Agriculture)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the monsoon and upper-air circulation:
1. The subtropical westerly jet stream shifts north of the Himalayas before the onset of the monsoon.
2. Western disturbances are carried by the tropical easterly jet.
3. A tropical easterly jet develops over peninsular India during the south-west monsoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In early summer the westerly jet withdraws from south of the Himalayas, which allows the ITCZ to move north and the monsoon to burst; the tropical easterly jet then helps the monsoon depressions. Western disturbances travel with the subtropical westerly jet in winter, not the easterly jet.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4; Certificate Physical Geography (G.C. Leong)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Western disturbances bring winter rainfall to north-western India that benefits the rabi wheat crop.
Statement-II: Western disturbances originate over the Mediterranean region and move eastwards with the subtropical westerly jet stream.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: These low-pressure systems pick up moisture over the Mediterranean and Caspian regions and are steered east by the westerly jet, giving light winter rain and snow in the north-west. The winter rain helps wheat, while the cloud cover also keeps nights warmer.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Tamil Nadu coast receives little rain during the south-west monsoon season.
Statement-II: The Tamil Nadu coast lies on the windward side of the Western Ghats.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The coast lies in the rain-shadow of the Western Ghats for the Arabian Sea branch and parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch, so it stays dry in summer. It gets most of its rain in October-December from the north-east monsoon, when winds blow in from the Bay of Bengal.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Match List-I (Local weather phenomenon) with List-II (Region) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Loo
B. Kalbaishakhi
C. Mango showers
D. Bardoli Chheerha
List-II
1. Assam
2. Kerala and Karnataka
3. Northern plains
4. West Bengal
questions.e: Loo is the hot, dry summer wind of the northern plains; Kalbaishakhi is the evening thunderstorm of West Bengal in April-May; mango showers help ripen mangoes in Kerala and Karnataka; Bardoli Chheerha is the Assam equivalent, helpful for tea.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the south-west monsoon:
1. The normal date of onset over Kerala is 1 June.
2. The normal date for the monsoon to cover the entire country is 8 July.
3. The withdrawal begins from the Gujarat coast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IMD's revised normal dates are 1 June for Kerala and 8 July for the whole country. Withdrawal starts from west Rajasthan (normal date 17 September), not from Gujarat.
questions.s: IMD; NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q: Pune receives much less rainfall than Mumbai in the monsoon season although they are at nearly the same latitude. What is the main reason?
o: Pune lies far north of the monsoon's path
Pune is not affected by the Arabian Sea branch because of the Aravalli Hills
Pune lies in the equatorial doldrums belt
Pune lies in the rain-shadow, leeward side of the Western Ghats
questions.e: Moist Arabian Sea winds shed most of their rain on the windward slopes of the Western Ghats, leaving descending, dry air for Pune. Mumbai lies on the windward side.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. La Nina is associated with deficient monsoon rainfall in India.
2. El Nino is the warming of surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.
3. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole generally favours good monsoon rainfall over India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: El Nino weakens the Walker circulation and usually reduces monsoon rain, while a positive IOD (warmer western Indian Ocean) tends to boost it and can offset El Nino. La Nina usually favours good monsoon rains, so statement 1 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 4; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many States of India?
questions.e: It passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies south of the line.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the drainage system of India:
1. The Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra are antecedent rivers.
2. The Narmada and Tapi flow eastwards through rift valleys into the Bay of Bengal.
3. The Narmada and Tapi form estuaries rather than deltas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Antecedent rivers kept their courses while the Himalaya rose across them. The Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea and form estuaries, because they flow through hard-rock rift valleys, carry little silt and have a short, steep course to the sea.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 3

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a left bank tributary of the Ganga?
questions.e: The Son flows from the Peninsular plateau and joins the Ganga on the right bank near Patna, like the Yamuna. Himalayan tributaries such as the Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi join from the left.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 3

questions.q:
The Alaknanda has five confluences (Prayags) before it becomes the Ganga. Arrange them in the order from upstream to downstream:
1. Devprayag
2. Rudraprayag
3. Vishnuprayag
4. Karnaprayag
5. Nandaprayag
questions.e: From the source: Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), Nandaprayag (Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Pindar), Rudraprayag (Mandakini), and Devprayag, where the Bhagirathi joins to form the Ganga.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 3
questions.h: Very Nice Kids Run Daily: V-N-K-R-D

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indus Waters Treaty:
1. It was signed in 1960.
2. The Jhelum and Chenab are classified as western rivers.
3. Under it, the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej were allocated to Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The treaty of 1960 gave the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India and the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan, with limited uses for India on the latter. Statement 3 reverses the allocation.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Drainage chapter; MEA

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Brahmaputra are correct?
1. It rises in Tibet where it is known as the Tsangpo.
2. It enters India in Assam as the Dihang.
3. The Lohit joins it near Sadiya in the Assam plain.
4. It is called the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
questions.e: It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the Siang or Dihang, and meets the Lohit and Dibang to be called the Brahmaputra in Assam. Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 3

questions.q:
Match List-I (River) with List-II (Place of origin) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Godavari
B. Krishna
C. Kaveri
D. Mahanadi
List-II
1. Brahmagiri hills
2. Trimbakeshwar
3. Mahabaleshwar
4. Sihawa range
questions.e: The Godavari rises near Trimbakeshwar (Nashik) and the Krishna at Mahabaleshwar, both in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra. The Kaveri rises in Brahmagiri (Kodagu, Karnataka) and the Mahanadi in the Sihawa range of Chhattisgarh.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 3

questions.q:
How many of the following lake-State pairs are correctly matched?
1. Chilika : Odisha
2. Sambhar : Gujarat
3. Loktak : Manipur
4. Wular : Himachal Pradesh
questions.e: Chilika (largest brackish-water lagoon) is in Odisha and Loktak in Manipur. Sambhar, a salt lake, is in Rajasthan, and Wular is in Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Drainage chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Luni river ends in the Arabian Sea.
2. The Mahi river crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
3. The Sabarmati river flows into the Gulf of Khambhat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Mahi rises in Madhya Pradesh, flows through Rajasthan and Gujarat and cuts the Tropic of Cancer twice in a curve. The Luni, from the Aravallis, loses itself in the marshes of the Rann of Kachchh and does not reach the sea.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 3; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Himalayan divisions:
1. The Himadri has the highest average elevation and permanent snow cover.
2. The Shiwaliks are the oldest and northernmost range of the Himalaya.
3. The Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) includes the Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar and Mahabharat ranges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Himalaya grows younger as one moves south: Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser) and Shiwaliks (outer). The Shiwaliks are the southernmost, youngest range, made of unconsolidated river deposits from the higher mountains.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2
questions.h: North to south: Himadri, Himachal, Shiwalik

questions.q:
Statement-I: Streams flowing from the Shiwaliks disappear in the Bhabar belt.
Statement-II: The Bhabar is a narrow belt of porous, pebble-rich deposits at the foothills, through which water sinks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Streams drop their coarse boulders and pebbles at the foothills, forming a permeable belt where water seeps underground. It re-emerges farther south in the marshy, finer Terai.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q: The Rohtang Pass, connecting Manali with Lahaul and Spiti, lies in which one of the following ranges?
questions.e: Rohtang, at nearly 4,000 m, crosses the Pir Panjal range, which divides the Beas valley from Lahaul. The Atal Tunnel under the pass now gives all-weather access.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2; PIB, Oct 2020

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about peaks in India are correct?
1. Kanchenjunga is the highest peak in India.
2. Nanda Devi is the highest peak lying entirely within India.
3. Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Western Ghats.
4. Anamudi is the highest peak of Peninsular India.
questions.e: Kanchenjunga (Sikkim-Nepal border, 8,586 m), Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand, 7,816 m) and Anamudi (Anaimalai hills, Kerala) are correct. Doddabetta (Nilgiris) is not the highest in the Western Ghats; Anamudi is higher, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Western and Eastern Ghats:
1. The Western Ghats are continuous and can be crossed only through passes.
2. The Nilgiri hills form the junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats.
3. The Eastern Ghats are higher and more continuous than the Western Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Western Ghats are higher and form an almost unbroken escarpment with passes such as Thal, Bhor and the Palghat Gap. The Eastern Ghats are lower and discontinuous, cut by the Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna and Kaveri.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chotanagpur plateau is a part of the Deccan lava plateau.
2. The Meghalaya plateau is an extension of the Peninsular plateau, separated from it by the Garo-Rajmahal gap.
3. The Deccan trap region is characterised by black soil formed by weathering of basalt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Deposition by the Ganga and Brahmaputra created the gap that detached the Meghalaya plateau. The Chotanagpur plateau is made of old crystalline rocks and is rich in minerals; it is not part of the volcanic Deccan trap.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Arrange the following coastal plains of the west coast from north to south:
1. Malabar coast
2. Konkan coast
3. Kannad coast
questions.e: The Konkan coast runs from Daman to Goa, the Kannad (Karnataka) coast from Goa to Mangalore, and the Malabar coast from Mangalore to Kanyakumari in Kerala.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian islands:
1. The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.
2. The Eight Degree Channel separates Kavaratti from Minicoy in Lakshadweep.
3. Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is the only confirmed active volcano in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives; Minicoy is separated from the rest of Lakshadweep by the Nine Degree Channel. Barren Island, near the Andaman group, is India's active volcano.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Kashmir valley is known for saffron cultivation.
Statement-II: The valley has Karewa lacustrine deposits, which are suited for saffron and almond.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Karewas are thick deposits of lake sediments laid in the valley when it held a large lake. Their well-drained, fertile soils support saffron, almond and walnut orchards.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment Ch 2
